**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ANO1 and calcium signaling in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets. Modulating calcium signaling pathways might offer a unified approach to treating aspects of both moyamoya disease and osteopetrosis, although the specific directional effects would require careful consideration.
